title: Persecution and Grace
english: …Thus they endured the persecution, even hiding in caves and rock crevices, prophets hiding, when also Elijah himself went up into a deep wilderness, but fell before God saying, 'Your altars they have demolished, Your prophets they have killed, and I alone am left, and they seek my soul'; but God answered immediately to this, 'I have left for myself seven thousand men who did not bend the knee to Baal.'

But just as then God was not the one causing the dreadful lawlessness in Israel, but they themselves were ruined by their own intentions, so again now, with God and Father offering salvation through Christ to all, and no one being persecuted, they willingly fell into apostasy, having rejected the Redeemer. Thus God did not reject His people, for He offered, as I said, if they would take a share in the salvation through Christ.

If by grace, it is no longer from works; for if it is from works, grace is no longer grace; for where someone thinks to be approved from works, there the name and thing of grace will be unnecessary and superfluous; for to the one working, the reward is not reckoned according to grace, but according to debt; thus if from works, it is no longer grace.

What then? What Israel seeks, it did not attain. He said that 'God did not reject His people'; since some were likely to object, they would say that God did reject His people, if Israel was lost, even if not completely, but in part; a remnant was saved, and this was by election. What Israel sought, it did not attain, but the elect did; the rest were hardened.

Israel sought justification by the law; but how was he to be justified, he says, when no one had completed the law? Thus Israel sought justification by type, but did not attain it; however, those who were cast out from the others through being lawless attained it; for they have been justified through faith, but the rest were hardened, that is, the hard and disobedient.

And David says, 'Let their table become a snare' (Psalm 69:23). He says, 'Let their table become a snare,' and the following: he provides for a proof of what he said a prophetic writing, not of one but of two prophets, so that 'by the mouth of two and three witnesses every word shall be established' (Matthew 18:16). For their table has become a snare most rightly, that is, their ill-hospitality and their hostility, which they have practiced against Christ during the time of His being crucified; for they offered Him vinegar mixed with gall; because of this, they were darkened in mind and look only downward, imagining things on the earth.
I say then, did they fall in order to perish? May it not be so. I marvel at your gentleness, oh divine Paul, for you handle the words of economy skillfully…
translator_notes: The text begins mid-sentence: '…Thus they endured...'
The text ends mid-sentence: '...handle the words of economy skillfully…'
The phrase 'no one had completed the law' translates 'τετελειωκότος οὐδένα τοῦ νόμου'.
